newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea wet Brent jumps up, other grades pressured.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea wet Brent jumps up, other grades pressured.

text.p: North Sea physical and paper Brent values leapt sharply on Wednesday, but traders said that abundant early March supplies were keeping a lid on differentials for other grades.

A Brent cargo loading March 6-8 traded at March Brent -2 cents after an end-February cargo fetched just March Brent -24 cents earlier in the day. Two early March cargoes were traded on Tuesday at March Brent -19 cents.
The March 6-8 Brent was one of two from the chains. It was kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline by a major and sold on to a Wall Street trader already holds two or three cargoes.
"I think (the buyer) would quite happily see Brent quotes higher," said one trader.

Brent CFDs also surged higher with next week (Feb 24-28) talked at April Brent +34/38 and the following week (March 3-7) at April +22/25 late in the day. April Brent paper was trading 29 cents up at $20.68 a barrel at 1840 GMT in line with the IPE screen.
Another trading house was bidding aggressively on CFDs and was also looking to pick up a wet Brent cargo, traders said.
But the bullish sentiment surrounding Brent was not shared by other North Sea grades.
It emerged on Wednesday that a cross-month Norwegian Oseberg traded earlier in the week at a soft Dated Brent -11 cents.
"It's a big drop in levels. Oseberg is really under pressure," said one trader.
March Oseberg was well offered at Dated Brent +30 cents, dealers said, but bid much lower.
